description:
FILED s451z, from the #703 probes.  PRE-EXISTING.

    my @c = readpipe("printf 'm\nn\n'");
        perl  runs the shell, 2 lines
        PCL   Undefined subroutine &main::readpipe called

perl spells every command capture `readpipe EXPR`, and the NAMED form is a
first-class builtin (t/op/exec.t rows 21-26 test it in both contexts, with the
default `$_` argument, and its argument's context).  PCL implements only the
`` `â¦` ``/`qx`/`` <<`` `` TERM (`p-backtick`); the name itself is unknown.

FIX SHAPE: `readpipe` is `p-backtick` with a spec of [0,1] in
`Pl/PExpr/Config.pm` and the `$_`-default family's -2 marker (`readpipe` with
no argument reads $_ -- exec.t:139).  Its LIST behaviour is #731, so land that
first or the new name inherits the same wrong answer.

BAR: t/op/exec.t rows 21-26 (scalar, list, default argument in both, and the
argument's own context); an overriding package (#703) must still win, because
`use subs "readpipe"` displaces the NAMED form too.
subject: `readpipe` is not a PCL builtin -- an explicit `readpipe(CMD)` call in a package with no such sub dies "Undefined subroutine"
